pairs: Pepigi fœdus cum oculis meis,
I reached an agreement with my eyes,
ut ne cogitarem quidem de virgine.
that I would not so much as think about a virgin.
Quam enim partem haberet in me Deus desuper,
For what portion should God from above hold for me,
et hæreditatem Omnipotens de excelsis?
and what inheritance should the Almighty from on high keep?
Numquid non perditio est iniquo,
Is not destruction held for the wicked
et alienatio operantibus injustitiam?
and repudiation kept for those who work injustice?
Nonne ipse considerat vias meas,
Does he not examine my ways
et cunctos gressus meos dinumerat?
and number all my steps?
Si ambulavi in vanitate,
If I have walked in vanity,
et festinavit in dolo pes meus,
or if my foot has hurried towards deceitfulness,
appendat me in statera justa,
let him weigh me in a just balance,
et sciat Deus simplicitatem meam.
and let God know my simplicity.
Si declinavit gressus meus de via,
If my steps have turned aside from the way,
et si secutum est oculos meos cor meum,
or if my heart has followed my eyes,
et si manibus meis adhæsit macula,
or if a blemish has clung to my hands,
seram,
then may I sow,
et alius comedat,
and let another consume,
et progenies mea eradicetur.
and let my offspring be eradicated.
Si deceptum est cor meum super muliere,
If my heart has been deceived over a woman,
et si ad ostium amici mei insidiatus sum,
or if I have waited in ambush at my friend’s door,
scortum alterius sit uxor mea,
then let my wife be the harlot of another,
et super illam incurventur alii.
and let other men lean over her.
Hoc enim nefas est,
For this is a crime
et iniquitas maxima.
and a very great injustice.
Ignis est usque ad perditionem devorans,
It is a fire devouring all the way to perdition,
et omnia eradicans genimina.
and it roots out all that springs forth.
Si contempsi subire judicium cum servo meo et ancilla mea,
If I have despised being subject to judgment with my servant or my maid,
cum disceptarent adversum me:
when they had any complaint against me,
quid enim faciam cum surrexerit ad judicandum Deus?
then what will I do when God rises to judge, and,
et cum quæsierit,
when he inquires,
quid respondebo illi?
how will I respond to him?
Numquid non in utero fecit me,
Is not he who created me in the womb,
qui et illum operatus est,
also he who labored to make him?
et formavit me in vulva unus?
And did not one and the same form me in the womb?
Si negavi quod volebant pauperibus,
If I have denied the poor what they wanted
et oculos viduæ expectare feci;
and have made the eyes of the widow wait;
si comedi buccellam meam solus,
if I have eaten my morsel of food alone,
et non comedit pupillus ex ea
while orphans have not eaten from it;
(quia ab infantia mea crevit mecum miseratio,
(for from my infancy mercy grew with me,
et de utero matris meæ egressa est mecum);
and it came out with me from my mother’s womb;)
si despexi pereuntem, eo quod non habuerit indumentum, et absque operimento pauperem;
if I have looked down on him who was perishing because he had no clothing and the poor without any covering,
si non benedixerunt mihi latera ejus,
if his sides have not blessed me,
et de velleribus ovium mearum calefactus est;
and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep;
si levavi super pupillum manum meam,
if I have lifted up my hand over an orphan,
etiam cum viderem me in porta superiorem:
even when it might seem to me that I have the advantage over him at the gate;
humerus meus a junctura sua cadat,
then may my shoulder fall from its joint,
et brachium meum cum suis ossibus confringatur.
and may my arm, with all its bones, be broken.
Semper enim quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Deum,
For I have always feared God, like waves flowing over me,
et pondus ejus ferre non potui.
whose weight I was unable to bear.
Si putavi aurum robur meum,
If I have considered gold to be my strength,
et obrizo dixi: Fiducia mea;
or if I have called purified gold ‘my Trust;’
si lætatus sum super multis divitiis meis,
if I have rejoiced over my great success,
et quia plurima reperit manus mea;
and over the many things my hand has obtained;
si vidi solem cum fulgeret,
if I gazed upon the sun when it shined
et lunam incedentem clare,
and the moon advancing brightly,
et lætatum est in abscondito cor meum,
so that my heart rejoiced in secret
et osculatus sum manum meam ore meo:
and I kissed my hand with my mouth,
quæ est iniquitas maxima,
which is a very great iniquity
et negatio contra Deum altissimum.
and a denial against the most high God;
Si gavisus sum ad ruinam ejus qui me oderat,
if I have been glad at the ruin of him who hated me
et exsultavi quod invenisset eum malum:
and have exulted that evil found him,
non enim dedi ad peccandum guttur meum, ut expeterem maledicens animam ejus.
for I have not been given my throat to sin by asking for a curse on his soul;
Si non dixerunt viri tabernaculi mei:
if the men around my tabernacle have not said:
Quis det de carnibus ejus,
“He might give us some of his food,
ut saturemur?
so that we will be filled,”
foris non mansit peregrinus:
for the foreigner did not remain at the door,
ostium meum viatori patuit.
my door was open to the traveler;
Si abscondi quasi homo peccatum meum, et celavi in sinu meo iniquitatem meam;
if, as man does, I have hidden my sin and have concealed my iniquity in my bosom;
si expavi ad multitudinem nimiam,
if I became frightened by an excessive crowd,
et despectio propinquorum terruit me:
and the disrespect of close relatives alarmed me,
et non magis tacui,
so that I would much rather have remained silent
nec egressus sum ostium.
or have gone out the door;
Quis mihi tribuat auditorem,
then, would he grant me a hearing,
ut desiderium meum audiat Omnipotens,
so that the Almighty would listen to my desire,
et librum scribat ipse qui judicat,
and he who judges would himself write a book,
ut in humero meo portem illum,
which I would then carry on my shoulder
et circumdem illum quasi coronam mihi?
and wrap around me like a crown?
Per singulos gradus meos pronuntiabo illum,
With each of my steps, I would pronounce and offer it,
et quasi principi offeram eum.
as if to a prince.
Si adversum me terra mea clamat,
So, if my land cries out against me,
et cum ipsa sulci ejus deflent:
and if its furrows weep with it,
si fructus ejus comedi absque pecunia, et animam agricolarum ejus afflixi:
if I have used its fruits for nothing but money and have afflicted the souls of its tillers,
pro frumento oriatur mihi tribulus,
then, may thistles spring forth for me instead of grain,
et pro hordeo spina.
and thorns instead of barley.
Finita sunt verba Job.
(This ended the words of Job.)
